			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">evaluating how well our executive compensation adheres to program objectives.</font></p></td></tr></table></div>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">To facilitate the delivery of these services to the Compensation Committee, Pearl Meyer interfaces with our management, primarily with our General Counsel and VP of Administration. In 2019, Pearl Meyer did not provide any services to the Company other than those requested by the Compensation Committee in Pearl Meyer&#x2019;s role as the Committee&#x2019;s independent advisor.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">Other than those services requested by the Compensation Committee, Pearl Meyer did not have any business or personal relationships with members of the Compensation Committee or executives of the Company, did not own any of the Company&#x2019;s common stock and maintained policies and procedures designed to avoid such conflicts of interest. As such, the Compensation Committee determined the engagement of Pearl Meyer in 2019 did not create any conflicts of interest.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Role of Executive Officers in Compensation Decisions</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">With respect to the compensation of the NEOs other than our Chief Executive Officer, the Compensation Committee considers the recommendations of our Chief Executive Officer and each NEO&#x2019;s individual performance. In light of our NEOs&#x2019; integral role in establishing and executing the Company&#x2019;s overall operational and financial objectives, the Compensation Committee requests that our NEOs provide the initial recommendations on the appropriate goals for the qualitative and quantitative performance metrics used in our short-term cash incentive program. However, the Committee is under no obligation to follow those recommendations, and only Compensation Committee members are allowed to vote on decisions regarding NEO compensation.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">The Compensation Committee may invite any NEO to attend Compensation Committee meetings to report on the Company&#x2019;s progress with respect to the annual quantitative and qualitative performance metrics, but any such officer is excluded from any decisions or discussions regarding his individual compensation.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, the Board has granted limited authority to Scott Bender, our Chief Executive Officer, to make awards under the LTIP to certain individuals who are not executive officers.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Role of Competitive Benchmarking</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">In the exercise of its duties, the Compensation Committee periodically evaluates the Company&#x2019;s executive compensation against that of comparable companies. The Compensation Committee does not set specific percentile goals against competitive data for purposes of determining executive compensation levels. In establishing individual compensation opportunities, the Committee considers this competitive data as well as a variety of other factors including individual performance, competencies, scope of responsibility, and internal equity.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">The Compensation Committee considers the competitive market to consist of the oilfield services industry broadly as well as other similarly sized companies in related industries who could potentially compete with us for executive talent. The Committee periodically reviews data for a selected peer group approved by the Compensation Committee (the &#x201C;peer group&#x201D;) as well as for broader general industry companies of comparable size and business complexity (compensation survey </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:8.82352941176471%;margin-right:8.82352941176471%;">

The selected peer companies are reviewed from time to time to ensure their continued appropriateness for comparative purposes.</font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:bold;">Elements of Compensation</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Base Salary</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">Base salary is the guaranteed element of an executive&#x2019;s direct compensation and is intended to provide a foundation for a competitive overall compensation opportunity for the executive. The Compensation Committee reviews each executive&#x2019;s base salary annually. Executive officer base salaries are determined after an evaluation that considers the executive&#x2019;s prior experience and breadth of knowledge and which also considers compensation data from peer group companies and other similarly sized companies in businesses comparable to the Company&#x2019;s, the Company&#x2019;s and the executive&#x2019;s performance, and any significant changes in the executive&#x2019;s responsibilities. The Compensation Committee considers all these factors together plus overall industry conditions. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt 0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">Salaries for our Chief Executive Officer and our Chief Operating Officer have remained unchanged since 2017. Effective February&nbsp;17, 2019, after discussions regarding competitive market data with Pearl Meyer, the Board approved a salary of $335,000 for Stephen Tadlock, who completed his transition to Chief Financial Officer on March&nbsp;15, 2019.</font>
		</p>

		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:22.3pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Short Term Incentives</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">Our NEOs are eligible for an annual incentive bonus which is designed to focus executives on execution of our annual plan, which is linked to our long-term strategy. Execution against our annual corporate plan is important to drive long-term shareholder value by improving financial strength, managing costs and investing in projects that will deliver future value. We employ financial and safety performance metrics to further specific objectives of our strategy, such as EBITDA and total recordable incident rate.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-style:italic;">Target Bonus Opportunity</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">For NEOs, the MIP has two performance parameters on which the bonus is calculated.&nbsp;&nbsp;The first parameter is Earnings Before Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortization, excluding exceptional items, as defined by the Board (EBITDA), which is weighted as 90% of the bonus opportunity.&nbsp;&nbsp;Participants begin to earn a bonus payout when EBITDA performance reaches Threshold EBITDA which is set at 80% of Target EBITDA.&nbsp;&nbsp;Participants are eligible for a Stretch bonus opportunity if actual EBITDA exceeds Target EBITDA.&nbsp;&nbsp;The maximum Stretch bonus payment is achieved when EBITDA performance reaches 120% of Target EBITDA.&nbsp;&nbsp;The maximum Stretch payment is 40% of the full, non-stretch bonus payment.&nbsp;&nbsp;The calculation of the EBITDA portion of the bonus payout is linear between Threshold and Target and between Target and Stretch.&nbsp;&nbsp;The second parameter is Total Recordable Incident Rate (&#x201C;TRIR&#x201D;) which is defined as the number of employees per 100 full-time employees that have been involved in a recordable injury or illness in the pertinent period.&nbsp;&nbsp;TRIR is weighted as 10% of the bonus opportunity.&nbsp;&nbsp;Participants begin to earn a bonus payout when TRIR performance reaches Threshold TRIR of 1.85.&nbsp;&nbsp;A full bonus payout on the TRIR parameter is achieved when safety performance reaches Target TRIR of 1.50 or lower.&nbsp;&nbsp;The calculation of the TRIR portion of the bonus payout is linear between Threshold and Target.&nbsp;&nbsp;Depending upon Company performance, actual payouts under the 2019 MIP may be between 0% and 140% of the Target Bonus opportunity for each NEO.</font>
		</p>

			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">Performance under the MIP is assessed relative to pre-established goals approved by the Committee near the beginning of the fiscal year. For 2019, the Compensation Committee approved performance objectives under the 2019 MIP after considering a combination of factors including alignment with the Company&#x2019;s business strategy, 2019 budget, investor expectations, recommendations from management, and the Committee&#x2019;s assessment of management&#x2019;s ability to impact outcomes. </font>

Based on this result, in addition to earning a full target bonus on the EBITDA component, executives also earned 40.1% of their 40% stretch opportunity an additional 16.2% of the full, non-stretch bonus calculation. The 2019 TRIR performance was 1.64 which is between Threshold and Target performance. Based on this performance NEOs were eligible for 59.2% payout on the TRIR parameter. In total, NEOs will receive a payout for the 2019 MIP of approximately&nbsp;111.3% of Target. 				</td>
			</tr>
		</table></div>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:22.3pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Long-Term Incentives</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">In order to incentivize individuals providing services to us or our affiliates, in 2018 the Board adopted a long&#8209;term incentive plan (the &#x201C;LTIP&#x201D;). The LTIP provides for the grant, from time to time, at the discretion of the Board or a committee thereof, of stock options, stock appreciation rights, restricted stock, restricted stock units, stock awards, dividend equivalents, other stock&#8209;based awards, cash awards, substitute awards and performance awards. </font><font style="display:inline;">The Board has delegated to the Compensation Committee the authority to administer the LTIP, including the power to determine the eligible individuals to whom awards will be granted, the number and type of awards to be granted and the terms and conditions of awards. </font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;"> In addition, the Board has granted limited authority to Scott Bender, our Chief Executive Officer, to make awards under the LTIP to certain individuals who are not executive officers. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">The primary purpose of awards under our LTIP is to enforce direct alignment between the long-term interests of our NEOs and those of our shareholders through the use of multi-year vesting and realized value of equity incentives that is contingent upon our stock price performance. Awards of equity under the LTIP also promote long-term share ownership by our NEOs, a goal which is further supported by the adoption of share ownership guidelines in 2019.</font><font style="display:inline;">&nbsp;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:8.82352941176471%;margin-right:8.82352941176471%;">

			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Retirement, Health and Welfare Benefits</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">The Company offers retirement, health and welfare benefits to substantially all of its U.S. employees including executive officers. Executive officers are eligible for these benefits on the same basis as other employees.&nbsp;&nbsp;Health and welfare benefits we offer to our employees include: medical, vision and dental coverage, life insurance, accidental death and dismemberment, short and long-term disability insurance, flexible spending accounts and employee assistance.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">The Company offers a defined contribution 401(k) retirement plan to substantially all of its U.S. employees, including the NEOs. Participants may contribute from 1% to 85% of their base pay and cash incentive compensation (subject to U.S. Internal Revenue Service (&#x201C;IRS&#x201D;) limitations), and the Company makes matching contributions under this plan on the first 7% of the participant&#x2019;s compensation (100% match of the first 3% employee contribution and 50% match on the next 4% employee contribution). Company matching contributions vest 20% per year on the first five anniversaries of the respective employee&#x2019;s hire date. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">We provide Scott Bender, Joel Bender, Stephen Tadlock, Steven Bender and Brian Small with bi-weekly vehicle allowances. Additionally, Scott Bender receives a gasoline reimbursement.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:12pt 0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:bold;">Other Compensation Practices and Policies</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Compensation Risk</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">Our compensation policies and practices are designed to provide rewards for short-term and long-term performance, both on an individual basis and at the entity level. In general, optimal financial and operational performance, particularly in a competitive business, requires some degree of risk-taking. Our compensation strategies are designed to encourage company growth and appropriate risk taking but not to encourage excessive risk taking. We also attempt to design the compensation program for our larger general employee population so that it does not inappropriately incentivize our employees to take unnecessary risks in their day to day activities. We recognize, however, that there are trade-offs and that it can be difficult in specific situations to maintain the appropriate balance. As such, we continue to evaluate our programs with a goal of preventing them from becoming materially imbalanced one way or the other.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">Our compensation arrangements contain certain design elements that are intended to minimize the incentive for taking unwarranted risk to achieve short-term, unsustainable results. Those elements include a maximum amount that can be earned under our annual incentive cash compensation program.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">We also provide compensation to our NEOs in the form of a reasonable base salary.&nbsp;&nbsp;We want our executives to be motivated to achieve Cactus&#x2019;s short-term and long-term goals, without sacrificing our financial and corporate integrity in trying to achieve those goals. While an executive&#x2019;s overall compensation should be strongly influenced by the achievement </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:8.82352941176471%;margin-right:8.82352941176471%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">78</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:8.82352941176471%;margin-right:8.82352941176471%;page-break-after:always;"><div style="background-color:#000000;clear:both;height:2pt;border:0;margin:30pt 0pt 30pt 0pt;"></div></div><div style="margin-left:8.82352941176471%;margin-right:8.82352941176471%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#TOC"><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:8.82352941176471%;margin-right:8.82352941176471%;"><p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">of specific financial and operational targets, we also believe that a portion of an executive&#x2019;s compensation should be awarded in components that provide a degree of financial certainty.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">In combination with our risk management practices, we do not believe that risks arising from our compensation policies and practices for our employees, including our NEOs, are reasonably likely to have a material adverse effect on us.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Clawback Policy</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<a name="_Hlk22910581"></a><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">In June 2019, our Board adopted the Executive Compensation Clawback Policy (the &#x201C;Clawback Policy&#x201D;). In the event of a restatement of our financial statements (other than a restatement caused by a change in applicable accounting rules or interpretations), the result of which is that any performance-based compensation paid under an incentive compensation plan would have been a lower amount had it been calculated based on such restated results, the Compensation Committee may seek to recover for the benefit of the Company the after tax portion of the difference between the compensation actually paid to the executive and the corrected amount based on the restated financial results.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

The Employment Agreements do not provide for accelerated or enhanced cash payments or health and welfare benefits upon a change in control but do provide for salary continuation payments and subsidized health and welfare benefits upon the termination of the executive&#x2019;s employment for &#x201C;good reason&#x201D; or without &#x201C;cause.&#x201D;&nbsp;&nbsp;Mr.&nbsp;Tadlock will be eligible to receive severance payments should a merger or sale transaction result in Mr.&nbsp;Tadlock being terminated by the new entity.&nbsp;&nbsp;In addition, Mr. Isaac will be eligible to receive severance payments should he be subject to a Qualifying Termination prior to the third anniversary of his commencement date.&nbsp;&nbsp;Severance payments that could become payable to Messrs.&nbsp;Scott and Joel Bender, Mr. Tadlock and Mr. Isaac pursuant to these arrangements have been described in more detail below under &#x201C;&#x2014;Potential Payments upon Termination or Change of Control&#x2014;Employment Agreements.&#x201D;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:22.5pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:bold;font-style:italic;">Non&#8209;Compete Agreements</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">In connection with our IPO, on February&nbsp;12, 2018, Cactus&nbsp;LLC entered into amended and restated noncompetition agreements (each, a &#x201C;Noncompetition Agreement&#x201D;) with each of Scott Bender and Joel Bender. Each of the Noncompetition Agreements provide that, for a period of one year following termination of his employment, Scott Bender and Joel Bender will not (i)&nbsp;compete against us in connection with our business, (ii)&nbsp;solicit or induce any of our employees to leave his or her employment with us or hire any of our employees or (iii)&nbsp;solicit or entice customers who were our customers within the one&#8209;year period immediately prior to his date of termination to cease doing business with us or to begin doing business with our competitors.&nbsp;&nbsp;Pursuant to his employment arrangement with the Company, Mr. Isaac is subject to the same restrictions. </font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-style:italic;">Scott Bender and Joel Bender Employment Agreements</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">We have entered into employment agreements with Messrs. Scott and Joel Bender.&nbsp;&nbsp;The Employment Agreements do not provide for accelerated or enhanced cash payments or health and welfare benefits upon a change in control but do provide for salary continuation payments and subsidized health and welfare benefits upon the termination of the executive&#x2019;s employment for &#x201C;good reason&#x201D; or without &#x201C;cause.&#x201D; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">To receive benefits under the Employment Agreements, the executive officer will be required to execute a release of all claims against the Company.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-style:italic;">Termination for Good Reason or Without Cause.</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;"> &nbsp;If either Scott or Joel Bender terminates his employment for &#x201C;good reason&#x201D; or is terminated by us without &#x201C;cause,&#x201D; he will be entitled to receive as severance, in addition to any amounts earned and unpaid through the date of termination, his then&#8209;current base salary and benefits (except car and expense reimbursement benefits) for the remaining term of the Employment Agreement if such term is greater than one year, or if such term is not greater than one year, one year from the date of termination, paid in lump sum within 60 days after the executive&#x2019;s separation from service.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-style:italic;">Termination Due to Disability.</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;"> &nbsp;If either Scott or Joel Bender&#x2019;s employment is terminated by either us or the executive due to disability, he will be entitled to receive as severance his then&#8209;current base salary and benefits through the remainder of the calendar month during which such termination is effective and for the lesser of (a)&nbsp;six consecutive months thereafter or (b)&nbsp;the date on which disability insurance benefits commence under any disability insurance coverage which may be provided by us, paid in lump sum within 30 days after the executive&#x2019;s termination due to disability.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-style:italic;">Termination Due to Death.</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;"> &nbsp;If either Scott or Joel Bender&#x2019;s employment is terminated due to death, his estate will be entitled to receive his then&#8209;current base salary and accrued benefits through the end of the calendar month in which his death occurs, paid in lump sum within 30 days after the executive&#x2019;s termination due to disability.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 9pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">In each case, if the executive is entitled to severance payments, during such severance period we will pay such executive&#x2019;s portion of Consolidated Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act (&#x201C;COBRA&#x201D;) premium payments, and if COBRA is no longer available during such period, we will provide similar health insurance coverage for such executive during the severance period.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">&#x2022;<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 12pt 0pt 0pt;"></font>The term &#x201C;good reason&#x201D; means any of the following: (i)&nbsp;we commit any material breach of the provisions of the executive&#x2019;s Employment Agreement; (ii)&nbsp;we assign the executive to a position, responsibilities or duties of a materially lesser status or degree of responsibility than his position, responsibilities or duties as of the effective date of the Employment Agreement; (iii)&nbsp;the requirement by us that the executive be based anywhere other than Houston, Texas, provided that such a change in geographic location be deemed material; or (iv)&nbsp;any decrease of more than 10% in the executive&#x2019;s base salary as of the effective date of the Employment Agreement. In any case, the executive must provide written notice of termination for good reason within 90&nbsp;days of the initial existence of the condition at issue, and we will have the opportunity to cure such circumstances within a 30&#8209;day period of receipt of such notice.</font>

			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">The Company&#x2019;s restricted stock unit award agreements provide that restricted stock awards will become fully vested on (i) the date a Change of Control occurs, (ii) the termination of an employee&#x2019;s employment due to his death or a Disability or (iii) upon the employee&#x2019;s Normal Retirement.&nbsp;&nbsp;As used in the restricted stock unit award agreements, &#x201C;Disability&#x201D; means that the employee is unable to perform the essential functions of their duties for three consecutive months, or three months during any six-month period, as determined after an examination by a medical doctor selected by written agreement of the employee and the Company.&nbsp;&nbsp;As used in the restricted stock unit award agreements, &#x201C;Normal Retirement&#x201D; means an employee&#x2019;s separation from service without Cause on or following the age of 65.&nbsp;&nbsp;For purposes of the restricted stock unit award agreements, &#x201C;Cause&#x201D; means the employee (i) is convicted of, or enters a </font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-style:italic;">nolo contendere</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;"> or guilty plea with respect to a crime involving fraud, theft, embezzlement or other act of material dishonesty, the Board&#x2019;s loss of confidence in the employee because he is convicted of or enters a </font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-style:italic;">nolo contendere</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;"> or guilty plea with respect to any felony or crime involving moral turpitude; (ii) commits any other material breach of any of the provisions of their employment agreement with the Company (if applicable) or any material employment contract, policy or agreement the employee has entered into with the Company, other than a breach which (being capable of being remedied) is remedied by the employee within fourteen days of being called upon to do so in writing by the Company; or (iii) fails to perform their duties and responsibilities (other than a failure resulting from Disability).&nbsp; </font>

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:bold;">2019 Chief Executive Officer Pay Ratio</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">As required by Section 953(b) of the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act, and Item 402(u) of Regulation S-K, we are providing the following information about the relationship of the median annual total compensation of our employees (other than the Chief Executive Officer) and the annual total compensation of Scott Bender, our Chief Executive Officer.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">For 2019, our last completed fiscal year:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 72pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Symbol;">&#xF0B7;<font style="display:inline;font-family:Symbol;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 12pt 0pt 0pt;"></font></font><font style="display:inline;">Scott Bender had total annual compensation of $2,163,931 as reflected in the Summary Compensation Table included in this Proxy Statement.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 108pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Courier New;">o<font style="display:inline;font-family:Courier New;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 12pt 0pt 0pt;"></font></font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">Our median employee&#x2019;s annual total compensation was $90,436.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 108pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Courier New;">o<font style="display:inline;font-family:Courier New;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 12pt 0pt 0pt;"></font></font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">As a result, we estimate that Scott Bender&#x2019;s 2019 annual total compensation was approximately 23.9 times that of our median employee.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 72pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Symbol;">&#xF0B7;<font style="display:inline;font-family:Symbol;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 12pt 0pt 0pt;"></font></font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">To identify the median employee, we took the following steps:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 108pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Courier New;">o<font style="display:inline;font-family:Courier New;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 12pt 0pt 0pt;"></font></font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">We determined that, as of December 1, 2019, our employee population consisted of 1,137 individuals. This population consisted of our full-time and part-time employees (including both active employees and employees on leave as of December 31, 2019);</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 108pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Courier New;">o<font style="display:inline;font-family:Courier New;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 12pt 0pt 0pt;"></font></font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">We selected December 1, 2019 as our identification date for determining our median employee because it enabled us to make such identification in a reasonably efficient and economic manner.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 108pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Courier New;">o<font style="display:inline;font-family:Courier New;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 12pt 0pt 0pt;"></font></font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">We used a consistently applied compensation measure to identify our median employee by comparing the actual amount of salary or wages as reflected in our payroll records. Compensation was annualized for employees that were not employed by us for all of 2019.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 108pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Courier New;">o<font style="display:inline;font-family:Courier New;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 12pt 0pt 0pt;"></font></font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">For our employees located outside of the United States, we obtained similar payroll records and converted such information into U.S. dollars using the year-end currency exchange rate.</font>

			<a href="#TOC"><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5pt 36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;">conversion rate adjustments for stock splits, stock dividends and reclassifications and other similar transactions, or (y)&nbsp;an equivalent amount of cash. Alternatively, upon the exercise of the Redemption Right, Cactus&nbsp;Inc. (instead of Cactus&nbsp;LLC) will have the right (the &#x201C;Call Right&#x201D;) to acquire each tendered CW Unit directly from the exchanging CW Unit Holder for, at its election, (x)&nbsp;one share of Class&nbsp;A Common Stock, subject to conversion rate adjustments for stock splits, stock dividends and reclassification and other similar transactions, or (y)&nbsp;an equivalent amount of cash. In connection with any redemption of CW Units pursuant to the Redemption Right or our Call Right, the corresponding number of shares of Class&nbsp;B Common Stock will be canceled. See &#x201C;Transactions with Related Persons&#x2014;Cactus Wellhead&nbsp;LLC Agreement.&#x201D; The amounts and percentages of common stock beneficially owned are reported on the basis of regulations of the SEC governing the determination of beneficial ownership of securities. Under the rules of the SEC, a person is deemed to be a &#x201C;beneficial owner&#x201D; of a security if that person has or shares voting power, which includes the power to vote or direct the voting of such security, or investment power, which includes the power to dispose of or to direct the disposition of such security. Securities that can be so acquired are deemed to be outstanding for purposes of computing such person&#x2019;s ownership percentage, but not for purposes of computing any other person&#x2019;s percentage. Under these rules, more than one person may be deemed a beneficial owner of the same securities, and a person may be deemed to be a beneficial owner of securities as to which such person has no economic interest. Except as otherwise indicated in these footnotes, each of the beneficial owners has, to our knowledge, sole voting and investment power with respect to the indicated shares of common stock, except to the extent this power may be shared with a spouse.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5pt 36pt;text-indent: -36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">(2)<font style="display:inline;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 27pt 0pt 0pt;"></font>Represents percentage of voting power of our Class&nbsp;A Common Stock and Class&nbsp;B Common Stock voting together as a single class. The CW Unit Holders hold one share of Class&nbsp;B Common Stock for each CW Unit that they own. Each share of Class&nbsp;B Common Stock has no economic rights but entitles the holder thereof to one vote for each CW Unit held by such holder. Accordingly, the CW Unit Holders collectively have a number of votes in Cactus&nbsp;Inc. equal to the number of CW&nbsp;Units that they hold.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 5pt 36pt;text-indent: -36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">(3)<font style="display:inline;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 27pt 0pt 0pt;"></font></font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">Cadent Energy Partners II,&nbsp;L.P., its general partner, Cadent Energy Partners II&#x2014;GP,&nbsp;L.P., and Cadent Management Services,&nbsp;LLC (&#x201C;Cadent Management&#x201D;), its manager, are indirectly controlled by Cadent Energy Partners. Cadent Energy Partners controls all voting and dispositive power over the reported shares and therefore may be deemed to be the beneficial owner of such shares. </font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;color:#000000;background-color: #FFFFFF;">Any decision taken by Cadent Management to vote, or to direct to vote, and to dispose, or to direct the disposition of, the securities held by Cadent has to be approved by its investment committee.&nbsp; There are four members of the investment committee, and unanimous approval of the members of the investment committee is required to approve an action.&nbsp; Under the so-called &#x201C;rule&nbsp;of three,&#x201D; if voting and dispositive decisions regarding an entity&#x2019;s securities are made by three or more individuals, and a voting or dispositive decision requires the approval of a majority of those individuals, then none of the individuals is deemed a beneficial owner of the entity&#x2019;s securities. This is the situation with regard to the investment committee of Cadent Management</font><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">. Bruce Rothstein, the Chairman of our board of directors, is a Managing Director of Cadent Energy Partners. Certain of our directors and officers have passive interests in Cadent. In connection with our IPO, Cactus&nbsp;Inc. entered into a Stockholders&#x2019; Agreement with Cadent and Cactus WH Enterprises, which provides Cadent and Cactus WH Enterprises with the right to designate a certain number of nominees to our board of directors so long as they and their respective affiliates collectively beneficially own at least 5% of the outstanding shares of our common stock. Therefore, Cadent and Cactus WH Enterprises may each be deemed to beneficially own an aggregate 26,281,822 shares of our Class B common stock, representing an aggregate combined voting power of 34.9%. Cadent also owns 5,264</font><font style="display:inline;"> shares of Class A common stock that was issued to Mr. Rothstein in connection with the vesting of previously granted restricted stock units. Due to Mr. Rothstein&#x2019;s position as a managing director at Cadent Energy Partners, all compensation and equity awards that he receives are directly payable or transferred to Cadent Management, a subsidiary of Cadent Energy Partners.</font>

In connection with our IPO, Cactus&nbsp;Inc. entered into a Stockholders&#x2019; Agreement with Cadent and </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-weight:bold;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times;">Item&nbsp;13.&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;</font><font style="display:inline;">Certain Relationships and Related Transactions, and Director Independence<a name="Item13CertainRelationshipsandRelatedTran"></a></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Policies and Procedures for Review of Related Party Transactions</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">A &#x201C;Related Party Transaction&#x201D; is a transaction, arrangement or relationship in which we or any of our subsidiaries was, is or will be a participant, the amount of which involved exceeds $120,000, and in which any related person had, has or will have a direct or indirect material interest. A &#x201C;Related Person&#x201D; means:</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&#x2022;<font style="display:inline;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 12pt 0pt 0pt;"></font>any person who is, or at any time during the applicable period was, one of our executive officers or one of our directors;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&#x2022;<font style="display:inline;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 12pt 0pt 0pt;"></font>any person who is known by us to be the beneficial owner of more than 5% of any class of our voting securities;</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&#x2022;<font style="display:inline;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 12pt 0pt 0pt;"></font>any immediate family member of any of the foregoing persons, which means any child, stepchild, parent, stepparent, spouse, sibling, mother&#8209;in&#8209;law, father&#8209;in&#8209;law, son&#8209;in&#8209;law, daughter&#8209;in&#8209;law, brother&#8209;in&#8209;law or sister&#8209;in&#8209;law of a director, executive officer or a beneficial owner of more than 5% of our Common Stock, and any person (other than a tenant or employee) sharing the household of such director, executive officer or beneficial owner of more than 5% of our Common Stock; and</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt 54pt;text-indent: -18pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">&#x2022;<font style="display:inline;;font-size: 10pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;text-indent:0pt;margin-left:0pt;padding:0pt 12pt 0pt 0pt;"></font>any firm, corporation or other entity in which any of the foregoing persons is a partner or principal or in a similar position or in which such person has a 10% or greater beneficial ownership interest.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Our board of directors adopted a written Related Party Transactions policy prior to the completion of our IPO. Pursuant to this policy, our Audit Committee has and will continue to review all material facts of all Related Party Transactions and either approve or disapprove entry into the Related Party Transaction, subject to certain limited exceptions. In determining whether to approve or disapprove entry into a Related Party Transaction, our Audit Committee takes into account, among other factors, the following: (i)&nbsp;whether the Related Party Transaction is on terms no less favorable than terms generally available to an unaffiliated third&nbsp;party under the same or similar circumstances and (ii)&nbsp;the extent of the Related Person&#x2019;s interest in the transaction. Further, the policy requires that all Related Party Transactions required to be disclosed in our filings with the SEC be so disclosed in accordance with applicable laws, rules and regulations.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Cactus Wellhead&nbsp;LLC Agreement</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Under the Cactus Wellhead&nbsp;LLC Agreement, each CW Unit Holder, subject to certain limitations, has the right, pursuant to the Redemption Right, to cause Cactus&nbsp;LLC to acquire all or at least a minimum portion of its CW Units for, at Cactus&nbsp;LLC&#x2019;s election, (x)&nbsp;shares of our Class&nbsp;A Common Stock at a redemption ratio of one share of Class&nbsp;A Common Stock for each CW Unit redeemed, subject to conversion rate adjustments for stock splits, stock dividends and reclassification and other similar transactions, or (y)&nbsp;an equivalent amount of cash. Alternatively, upon the exercise of the Redemption Right, Cactus&nbsp;Inc. (instead of Cactus&nbsp;LLC) will have the right, pursuant to the Call Right, to acquire each tendered CW Unit directly from the exchanging CW Unit Holder for, at its election, (x)&nbsp;one share of Class&nbsp;A Common Stock, subject to conversion rate adjustments for stock splits, stock dividends and reclassifications and other similar transactions, or (y)&nbsp;an equivalent amount of cash. In connection with any redemption of CW Units pursuant to the Redemption Right or our Call Right, the corresponding number of shares of Class&nbsp;B Common Stock will be canceled. In addition, any redemptions involving all of the CW Units held by a CW Unit Holder (subject to the discretion of Cactus&nbsp;Inc. to restrict redemptions of a lower number of units) may occur at any time. As the CW Unit Holders redeem their CW Units, our membership interest in Cactus&nbsp;LLC will be correspondingly increased, the number of shares of Class&nbsp;A Common Stock outstanding will be increased, and the number of shares of Class&nbsp;B Common Stock outstanding will be reduced.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;"></font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">94</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;page-break-after:always;"><div style="background-color:#000000;clear:both;height:2pt;border:0;margin:30pt 0pt 30pt 0pt;"></div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#TOC"><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;"></font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Under the Cactus Wellhead&nbsp;LLC Agreement, we have the right to determine when distributions will be made to CW Unit Holders and the amount of any such distributions. If we authorize a distribution, such distribution will be made to the holders of CW Units on a pro rata basis in accordance with their respective percentage ownership of CW Units.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The holders of CW Units, including us, will generally incur U.S. federal, state and local income taxes on their proportionate share of any taxable income of Cactus&nbsp;LLC and will be allocated their proportionate share of any taxable loss of Cactus&nbsp;LLC. Net profits and net losses of Cactus&nbsp;LLC generally will be allocated to holders of CW Units on a pro rata basis in accordance with their respective percentage ownership of CW Units, except that certain non pro rata adjustments will be required to be made to reflect built-in gains and losses and tax depletion, depreciation and amortization with respect to such built-in gains and losses. To the extent Cactus&nbsp;LLC has available cash and subject to the terms of any current or future credit agreements or debt instruments, we intend to cause Cactus&nbsp;LLC to make (i) pro rata distributions to the holders of CW Units, including us, in an amount at least sufficient to allow us to pay our taxes and make payments under the Tax Receivable Agreement that we entered into with the TRA Holders in connection with our IPO and (ii)&nbsp;non pro rata payments to Cactus&nbsp;Inc. to reimburse us for our corporate and other overhead expenses incurred by us in connection with serving as a managing member of Cactus&nbsp;LLC.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">The Cactus Wellhead&nbsp;LLC Agreement provides that, except as otherwise determined by us, at any time we issue a share of our Class&nbsp;A Common Stock or any other equity security, the net proceeds received by us with respect to such issuance, if any, shall be concurrently invested in Cactus&nbsp;LLC, and Cactus&nbsp;LLC shall issue to us one CW Unit or other economically equivalent equity interest. Conversely, if at any time, any shares of our Class&nbsp;A Common Stock are redeemed, repurchased or otherwise acquired, Cactus&nbsp;LLC shall redeem, repurchase or otherwise acquire an equal number of CW Units held by us, upon the same terms and for the same price, as the shares of our Class&nbsp;A Common Stock are redeemed, repurchased or otherwise acquired.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Under the Cactus Wellhead&nbsp;LLC Agreement, Cadent and its affiliates are not required to offer to us an opportunity to participate in specified business opportunities that are from time to time presented to Cadent and its affiliates, including any of our directors affiliated with Cadent. The Cactus Wellhead&nbsp;LLC Agreement further provides that if Cadent or an affiliate, including any of our directors affiliated with Cadent, becomes aware of a potential business opportunity, transaction or other matter, they will have no duty to communicate or offer that opportunity to us (unless such opportunity is expressly offered to such director in his capacity as one of our directors). In addition, the Cactus Wellhead&nbsp;LLC Agreement provides that none of Cadent and its affiliates, including any of our directors affiliated with Cadent, will have any duty to refrain from (i)&nbsp;engaging in a corporate opportunity in the same or similar lines of business in which we or our affiliates now engage or propose to engage or (ii)&nbsp;otherwise competing with us or our affiliates.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;">Cactus&nbsp;LLC will be dissolved only upon the first to occur of (i)&nbsp;the sale of substantially all of its assets or (ii)&nbsp;an election by us to dissolve the company. Upon dissolution, Cactus&nbsp;LLC will be liquidated and the proceeds from any liquidation will be applied and distributed in the following manner: (a)&nbsp;first, to creditors (including to the extent permitted by law, creditors who are members) in satisfaction of the liabilities of Cactus&nbsp;LLC, (b)&nbsp;second, to establish cash reserves for contingent or unforeseen liabilities and (c)&nbsp;third, to the members in proportion to the number of CW Units owned by each of them.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-weight:bold;">Tax Receivable Agreement</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">Pursuant to the Cactus Wellhead LLC Agreement, each TRA Holder will, subject to certain limitations, have the right (the &#x201C;Redemption Right&#x201D;) to cause Cactus LLC to acquire all or at least a minimum portion of its CW Units for, at Cactus LLC&#x2019;s election, (x) shares of our Class A common stock at a redemption ratio of one share of Class A common stock for each CW Unit redeemed, subject to conversion rate adjustments for stock splits, stock dividends and reclassification and other similar transactions, or (y) an equivalent amount of cash. Alternatively, upon the exercise of the Redemption Right, Cactus Inc. (instead of Cactus LLC) will have the right (the &#x201C;Call Right&#x201D;) to acquire each tendered CW Unit directly from the exchanging TRA Holder for, at its election, (x) one share of Class A common stock, </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">95</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;page-break-after:always;"><div style="background-color:#000000;clear:both;height:2pt;border:0;margin:30pt 0pt 30pt 0pt;"></div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#TOC"><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">subject to conversion rate adjustments for stock splits, stock dividends and reclassifications and other similar transactions, or (y) an equivalent amount of cash. In connection with any redemption of CW Units pursuant to the Redemption Right or our Call Right, the corresponding number of shares of Class B common stock will be canceled. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">Cactus LLC has made for itself (and for each of its direct or indirect subsidiaries that is treated as a partnership for U.S. federal income tax purposes and that it controls) an election under Section 754 of the Internal Revenue Code (the &#x201C;Code&#x201D;) that will be effective for 2018 and each taxable year in which a redemption of CW Units pursuant to the Redemption Right or the Call Right occurs. Pursuant to the Section 754 election, redemptions of CW Units pursuant to the Redemption Right or the Call Right are expected to result in adjustments to the tax basis of the tangible and intangible assets of Cactus LLC. These adjustments will be allocated to Cactus Inc. Such adjustments to the tax basis of the tangible and intangible assets of Cactus LLC would not have been available to Cactus Inc. absent its acquisition or deemed acquisition of CW Units pursuant to the exercise of the Redemption Right or the Call Right. In addition, the repayment of borrowings outstanding under the Cactus LLC term loan facility resulted in adjustments to the tax basis of the tangible and intangible assets of Cactus LLC, a portion of which was allocated to Cactus Inc. </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">These basis adjustments are expected to increase (for tax purposes) Cactus Inc.&#x2019;s depreciation and amortization deductions and may also decrease Cactus Inc.&#x2019;s gains (or increase its losses) on future dispositions of certain assets to the extent tax basis is allocated to those assets. Such increased deductions and losses and reduced gains may reduce the amount of tax that Cactus Inc. would otherwise be required to pay in the future.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">The TRA will generally provide for the payment by Cactus Inc. to each TRA Holder of 85% of the net cash savings, if any, in U.S. federal, state and local income tax and franchise tax that Cactus Inc. actually realizes or is deemed to realize in certain circumstances as a result of (i) certain increases in tax basis that occur as a result of Cactus Inc.&#x2019;s acquisition (or deemed acquisition for U.S. federal income tax purposes) of all or a portion of such TRA Holder&#x2019;s CW Units in connection with CW Unit exchanges or pursuant to the exercise of the Redemption Right or the Call Right, (ii) certain increases in tax basis resulting from the repayment of borrowings outstanding under Cactus LLC&#x2019;s term loan facility and (iii) imputed interest deemed to be paid by Cactus Inc. as a result of, and additional tax basis arising from, any payments Cactus Inc. makes under the TRA. We will retain the benefit of the remaining 15% of the cash savings.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">The payment obligations under the TRA are Cactus Inc.&#x2019;s obligations and not obligations of Cactus LLC, and we expect that the payments we will be required to make under the TRA will be substantial. We have determined that it is more likely than not that actual cash tax savings will be realized by Cactus Inc. from the tax benefits resulting from our IPO (and the related transactions), the follow-on equity offering in July 2018 and March 2019 and CW Unit exchanges. Future exchanges of CW Units create additional liability and follow the same accounting procedures. Estimating the amount and timing of payments that may become due under the TRA is by its nature imprecise and the assumptions used in the estimate can change. For purposes of the TRA, net cash savings in tax generally will be calculated by comparing Cactus Inc.&#x2019;s actual tax liability (determined by using the actual applicable U.S. federal income tax rate and an assumed combined state and local income tax rate) to the amount it would have been required to pay had it not been able to utilize any of the tax benefits subject to the TRA. The amounts payable, as well as the timing of any payments under the TRA, are dependent upon significant future events and assumptions, including the timing of the redemption of CW Units, the price of our Class A common stock at the time of each redemption, the extent to which such redemptions are taxable transactions, the amount of the redeeming unit holder&#x2019;s tax basis in its CW Units at the time of the relevant redemption, the depreciation and amortization periods that apply to the increase in tax basis, the amount and timing of taxable income we generate in the future and the U.S. federal income tax rate then applicable, and the portion of Cactus Inc.&#x2019;s payments under the TRA that constitute imputed interest or give rise to depreciable or amortizable tax basis.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">A delay in the timing of redemptions of CW Units, holding other assumptions constant, would be expected to decrease the discounted value of the amounts payable under the TRA as the benefit of the depreciation and amortization deductions would be delayed and the estimated increase in tax basis could be reduced as a result of allocations of Cactus </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">96</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;page-break-after:always;"><div style="background-color:#000000;clear:both;height:2pt;border:0;margin:30pt 0pt 30pt 0pt;"></div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#TOC"><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">LLC taxable income to the redeeming unit holder prior to the redemption. Stock price increases or decreases at the time of each redemption of CW Units would be expected to result in a corresponding increase or decrease in the undiscounted amounts payable under the TRA in an amount equal to 85% of the tax-effected change in price. The amounts payable under the TRA are dependent upon Cactus Inc. having sufficient future taxable income to utilize the tax benefits on which it is required to make payments under the TRA. If Cactus Inc.&#x2019;s projected taxable income is significantly reduced, the expected payments would be reduced to the extent such tax benefits do not result in a reduction of Cactus Inc.&#x2019;s future income tax liabilities.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">It is possible that future transactions or events could increase or decrease the actual tax benefits realized and the corresponding liability from the TRA. Moreover, there may be a negative impact on our liquidity if, as a result of timing discrepancies or otherwise, (i) the payments under the TRA exceed the actual benefits we realize in respect of the tax attributes subject to the TRA or (ii) distributions to Cactus Inc. by Cactus LLC are not sufficient to permit Cactus Inc. to make payments under the TRA after it has paid its taxes and other obligations. The payments under the TRA will not be conditional on a holder of rights under the TRA having a continued ownership interest in either Cactus LLC or Cactus Inc.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">In addition, although we are not aware of any issue that would cause the Internal Revenue Service (&#x201C;IRS&#x201D;) or other relevant tax authorities to challenge potential tax basis increases or other tax benefits covered under the TRA, the TRA Holders will not reimburse us for any payments previously made under the TRA if such basis increases or other benefits are subsequently disallowed, except that excess payments made to any such holder will be netted against payments otherwise to be made, if any, to such holder after our determination of such excess. As a result, in such circumstances, Cactus Inc. could make payments that are greater than its actual cash tax savings, if any, and may not be able to recoup those payments.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">The term of the TRA commenced upon completion of our IPO and will continue until all tax benefits that are subject to the TRA have been utilized or expired, unless we exercise our right to terminate the TRA. In the event that the TRA is not terminated, the payments under the TRA, which commenced in 2019, will continue for approximately 20 years after the date of the last redemption of CW Units. Accordingly, it is expected that payments will continue to be made under the TRA for more than 20 years. If we elect to terminate the TRA early (or it is terminated early due to certain mergers, asset sales, other forms of business combinations or other changes of control), our obligations under the TRA would accelerate and we would be required to make an immediate payment equal to the present value of the anticipated future payments to be made by us under the TRA (determined by applying a discount rate of one-year LIBOR plus 150 basis points) and such payment is expected to be substantial. The calculation of anticipated future payments will be based upon certain assumptions and deemed events set forth in the TRA, including the assumptions that (i) we have sufficient taxable income to fully utilize the tax benefits covered by the TRA and (ii) any CW Units (other than those held by Cactus Inc.) outstanding on the termination date are deemed to be redeemed on the termination date. Any early termination payment may be made significantly in advance of the actual realization, if any, of the future tax benefits to which the termination payment relates. Assuming no material changes in the relevant tax law, we expect that if the TRA were terminated as of December 31, 2019, the estimated termination payments, based on the assumptions discussed above, would be approximately $331.3</font><font style="display:inline;"> million (calculated using a discount rate equal to one-year LIBOR plus 150 basis points, applied against an undiscounted liability of $434.7 million). A 10% increase in the price of our Class A Common Stock at December 31, 2019 would have increased the discounted liability by $17.2 million to $348.5 million (an undiscounted increase of $23.2 million to $457.9 million), and likewise, a 10% decrease in the price of our Class A Common Stock at December 31, 2019 would have decreased the discounted liability by $17.3 million to $314.0 million (an undiscounted decrease of $23.3 million to $411.4 million).</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">The TRA provides that in the event that we breach any of our material obligations under the TRA, whether as a result of (i) our failure to make any payment when due (including in cases where we elect to terminate the TRA early, the TRA is terminated early due to certain mergers, asset sales, or other forms of business combinations or changes of control or we have available cash but fail to make payments when due under circumstances where we do not have the </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">97</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;page-break-after:always;"><div style="background-color:#000000;clear:both;height:2pt;border:0;margin:30pt 0pt 30pt 0pt;"></div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 30pt;color:#0563C1;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<a href="#TOC"><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;color:#0563C1;">Table of Contents</font></a>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;"><font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">right to elect to defer the payment, as described below), (ii) our failure to honor any other material obligation under it or (iii) by operation of law as a result of the rejection of the TRA in a case commenced under the U.S. Bankruptcy Code or otherwise, then the TRA Holders may elect to treat such breach as an early termination, which would cause all our payment and other obligations under the TRA to be accelerated and become due and payable applying the same assumptions described above.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">As a result of either an early termination or a change of control, we could be required to make payments under the TRA that exceed our actual cash tax savings under the TRA. In these situations, our obligations under the TRA could have a substantial negative impact on our liquidity and could have the effect of delaying, deferring or preventing certain mergers, asset sales, or other forms of business combinations or changes of control.&nbsp; </font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">Decisions we make in the course of running our business, such as with respect to mergers, asset sales, other forms of business combinations or other changes in control, may influence the timing and amount of payments that are received by the TRA Holders under the TRA. For example, the earlier disposition of assets following a redemption of CW Units may accelerate payments under the TRA and increase the present value of such payments, and the disposition of assets before a redemption of CW Units may increase the TRA Holders&#x2019; tax liability without giving rise to any rights of the TRA Holders to receive payments under the TRA. Such effects may result in differences or conflicts of interest between the interests of the TRA Holders and other shareholders.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">Payments generally are due under the TRA within five business days following the finalization of the schedule with respect to which the payment obligation is calculated. However, interest on such payments will begin to accrue from the due date (without extensions) of our U.S. federal income tax return for the period to which such payments relate until such payment date at a rate equal to one-year LIBOR plus 150 basis points. Except in cases where we elect to terminate the TRA early or it is otherwise terminated as described above, generally we may elect to defer payments due under the TRA if we do not have available cash to satisfy our payment obligations under the TRA. Any such deferred payments under the TRA generally will accrue interest from the due date for such payment until the payment date at a rate of one-year LIBOR plus 550 basis points. However, interest will accrue from the due date for such payment until the payment date at a rate of one-year LIBOR plus 150 basis points if we are unable to make such payment as a result of limitations imposed by our credit facility. We have no present intention to defer payments under the TRA.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">Because we are a holding company with no operations of our own, our ability to make payments under the TRA is dependent on the ability of Cactus LLC to make distributions to us in an amount sufficient to cover our obligations under the TRA. This ability, in turn, may depend on the ability of Cactus LLC&#x2019;s subsidiaries to make distributions to it. The ability of Cactus LLC, its subsidiaries and other entities in which it directly or indirectly holds an equity interest to make such distributions will be subject to, among other things, the applicable provisions of Delaware law (or other applicable jurisdiction) that may limit the amount of funds available for distribution and restrictions in relevant debt instruments issued by Cactus LLC or its subsidiaries and other entities in which it directly or indirectly holds an equity interest. Additionally, distributions made by Cactus LLC generally require pro-rata distribution among all its members, which could be significant. To the extent that we are unable to make payments under the TRA for any reason, such payments will be deferred and will accrue interest until paid.</font>
		</p>
		<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12pt;text-indent:36pt;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">
			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">Two of our independent directors, Messrs. McGovern and O&#x2019;Donnell, have the right to receive payments under the Tax Receivable Agreement in respect of CW Units owned by them at the time of our IPO.&nbsp;During 2019, a company controlled by Scott Bender and Joel Bender received approximately $2.1 million in payments under the TRA in respect </font></p></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;">
		<p><font size="1"> </font></p><div style="width:100%">

		<p style="margin:24pt 0pt 0pt;text-align:center;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;font-size: 10pt;">

			<font style="display:inline;font-family:Times New Roman,Times,serif;">98</font>

		</p>

</div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;page-break-after:always;"><div style="background-color:#000000;clear:both;height:2pt;border:0;margin:30pt 0pt 30pt 0pt;"></div></div><div style="margin-left:10.2941176470588%;margin-right:10.2941176470588%;"><div style="width:100%">
